messages.content: what's the color of the sea?

function.name: generate_sea_foam
function.description: Simulates the creation of sea foam based on the agitation level of water, amount of organic material, and the presence of salt. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

agitation_level.description: The level of agitation in the water, represented by a scale from 1 (calm) to 10 (very agitated).

organic_material.description: The amount of organic material present in grams per liter. This is a float type value.

salt_presence.description: Indicates whether salt is present (true) or not (false) in the water.

temperature.description: The water temperature in degrees Celsius. If unspecified, defaults to average sea temperature. This is a float type value.

message.content: The color of the sea can vary widely depending on several factors such as depth, clarity, presence of algae, sediment, and light conditions. In general, shallow waters often appear turquoise or greenish-blue due to reflection of sunlight and scattering by water molecules. Deeper waters tend to look darker blue or even black because more light is absorbed. Coastal areas may have a milky white appearance if there’s a lot of suspended sediment or algae. So while “blue” is the most common descriptor, the actual hue can range from bright turquoise to deep navy, sometimes with green or even brownish tints.
message.reasoning: The user asks "what's the color of the sea?" We need to respond with an answer. There's no tool needed. Just give a descriptive answer.
